entries.text: The product enables components that contain untrusted firmware before memory and fabric access controls have been enabled.

entries.name: ASP.NET Misconfiguration: Missing Custom Error Page
entries.text: An ASP .NET application must enable custom error pages in order to prevent attackers from mining information from the framework's built-in responses.

entries.name: Classic Buffer Overflow
entries.title: Buffer Copy without Checking Size of Input
entries.text: The product copies an input buffer to an output buffer without verifying that the size of the input buffer is less than the size of the output buffer.

entries.name: Generation of Weak Initialization Vector (IV)
entries.text: The product uses a cryptographic primitive that uses an Initialization Vector (IV), but the product does not generate IVs that are sufficiently unpredictable or unique according to the expected cryptographic requirements for that primitive.

entries.name: Failure to Disable Reserved Bits
entries.text: The reserved bits in a hardware design are not disabled prior to production.

entries.name: Stack-based Buffer Overflow
entries.text: The product writes past the end of a buffer that was allocated on the stack.

entries.name: Heap-based Buffer Overflow
entries.text: The product writes past the end of a buffer that was allocated on the heap.

entries.name: Insufficient Granularity of Access Control
entries.text: The product implements access controls via a policy or other feature with the intention to disable or restrict accesses (reads and/or writes) to assets in a system from untrusted agents. However, implemented access controls lack the required granularity

entries.name: Incorrect Register Defaults or Module Parameters
entries.text: Hardware description language code incorrectly defines register defaults or hardware Intellectual Property (IP) parameters to insecure values.
terms: Incorrect Register Defaults or Module Parameters

entries.name: Insufficient Granularity of Address Regions Protected by Register Locks
entries.text: The product defines a large address region protected from modification by the same register lock control bit. This results in a conflict between the functional requirement that some addresses need to be writable by software during operation and the security requirement that the system configuration lock bit must be set during the boot process.

entries.name: Race Condition for Write-Once Attributes
entries.text: A write-once register in hardware design is programmable by an untrusted software component earlier than the trusted software component, resulting in a race condition issue.

entries.name: Improper Restriction of Write-Once Bit Fields
entries.text: The hardware design control register "sticky bits" or write-once bit fields are improperly implemented, such that they can be reprogrammed by software.

entries.name: Creation of Emergent Resource
entries.text: The product manages resources or behaves in a way that indirectly creates a new, distinct resource that can be used by attackers in violation of the intended policy.

entries.name: Write-what-where Condition
entries.text: Any condition where the attacker has the ability to write an arbitrary value to an arbitrary location, often as the result of a buffer overflow.

entries.name: Exposure of Sensitive Information Through Metadata
entries.text: The product prevents direct access to a resource containing sensitive information, but it does not sufficiently limit access to metadata that is derived from the original, sensitive information.
terms: Exposure of Sensitive Information Through Metadata

entries.name: Improper Prevention of Lock Bit Modification
entries.text: The product uses a trusted lock bit for restricting access to registers, address regions, or other resources, but the product does not prevent the value of the lock bit from being modified after it has been set.
terms: Improper Prevention of Lock Bit Modification

entries.name: Improper Lock Behavior After Power State Transition
entries.text: Register lock bit protection disables changes to system configuration once the bit is set. Some of the protected registers or lock bits become programmable after power state transitions (e.g., Entry and wake from low power sleep modes) causing the system configuration to be changeable.

entries.name: Security-Sensitive Hardware Controls with Missing Lock Bit Protection
entries.text: The product uses a register lock bit protection mechanism, but it does not ensure that the lock bit prevents modification of system registers or controls that perform changes to important hardware system configuration.

entries.name: Hardware Internal or Debug Modes Allow Override of Locks
entries.text: System configuration protection may be bypassed during debug mode.

entries.name: Incorrect Use of Autoboxing and Unboxing for Performance Critical Operations
entries.text: The code uses boxed primitives, which may introduce inefficiencies into performance-critical operations.

entries.name: CSV Injection
entries.title: Improper Neutralization of Formula Elements in a CSV File
entries.text: The product saves user-provided information into a Comma-Separated Value (CSV) file, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special elements that could be interpreted as a command when the file is opened by a spreadsheet product.

entries.name: Improper Zeroization of Hardware Register
entries.text: The hardware product does not properly clear sensitive information from built-in registers when the user of the hardware block changes.

entries.name: Buffer Underwrite
entries.text: The product writes to a buffer using an index or pointer that references a memory location prior to the beginning of the buffer.

entries.name: Use of a Cryptographic Primitive with a Risky Implementation
entries.text: To fulfill the need for a cryptographic primitive, the product implements a cryptographic algorithm using a non-standard, unproven, or disallowed/non-compliant cryptographic implementation.

entries.name: Use of Predictable Algorithm in Random Number Generator
entries.text: The device uses an algorithm that is predictable and generates a pseudo-random number.

entries.name: Inclusion of Undocumented Features or Chicken Bits
entries.text: The device includes chicken bits or undocumented features that can create entry points for unauthorized actors.

entries.name: Sensitive Non-Volatile Information Not Protected During Debug
entries.text: Access to security-sensitive information stored in fuses is not limited during debug.

entries.name: Internal Asset Exposed to Unsafe Debug Access Level or State
entries.text: The product uses physical debug or test interfaces with support for multiple access levels, but it assigns the wrong debug access level to an internal asset, providing unintended access to the asset from untrusted debug agents.

entries.name: Improper Finite State Machines (FSMs) in Hardware Logic
entries.text: Faulty finite state machines (FSMs) in the hardware logic allow an attacker to put the system in an undefined state, to cause a denial of service (DoS) or gain privileges on the victim's system.

entries.name: Improper Write Handling in Limited-write Non-Volatile Memories
entries.text: The product does not implement or incorrectly implements wear leveling operations in limited-write non-volatile memories.

entries.name: Improper Protection Against Voltage and Clock Glitches
entries.text: The device does not contain or contains incorrectly implemented circuitry or sensors to detect and mitigate voltage and clock glitches and protect sensitive information or software contained on the device.

entries.name: Semiconductor Defects in Hardware Logic with Security-Sensitive Implications
entries.text: The security-sensitive hardware module contains semiconductor defects.

entries.name: Ghost in the Shell
entries.title: Application-Level Admin Tool with Inconsistent View of Underlying Operating System
entries.text: The product provides an application for administrators to manage parts of the underlying operating system, but the application does not accurately identify all of the relevant entities or resources that exist in the OS; that is, the application's model of the OS's state is inconsistent with the OS's actual state.

entries.name: Out-of-bounds Read
entries.text: The product reads data past the end, or before the beginning, of the intended buffer.

entries.name: Improper Preservation of Consistency Between Independent Representations of Shared State
entries.text: The product has or supports multiple distributed components or sub-systems that are each required to keep their own local copy of shared data - such as state or cache - but the product does not ensure that all local copies remain consistent with each other.

entries.name: Mirrored Regions with Different Values
entries.text: The product's architecture mirrors regions without ensuring that their contents always stay in sync.

entries.name: CPU Hardware Not Configured to Support Exclusivity of Write and Execute Operations
entries.text: The CPU is not configured to provide hardware support for exclusivity of write and execute operations on memory. This allows an attacker to execute data from all of memory.

entries.name: Incorrect Selection of Fuse Values
entries.text: The logic level used to set a system to a secure state relies on a fuse being unblown.

entries.name: Incorrect Comparison Logic Granularity
entries.text: The product's comparison logic is performed over a series of steps rather than across the entire string in one operation. If there is a comparison logic failure on one of these steps, the operation may be vulnerable to a timing attack that can result in the interception of the process for nefarious purposes.

entries.name: Comparison Logic is Vulnerable to Power Side-Channel Attacks
entries.text: A device's real time power consumption may be monitored during security token evaluation and the information gleaned may be used to determine the value of the reference token.

entries.name: Improper Restriction of Software Interfaces to Hardware Features
entries.text: The product provides software-controllable device functionality for capabilities such as power and clock management, but it does not properly limit functionality that can lead to modification of hardware memory or register bits, or the ability to observe physical side channels.

entries.name: Improper Access Control Applied to Mirrored or Aliased Memory Regions
entries.text: Aliased or mirrored memory regions in hardware designs may have inconsistent read/write permissions enforced by the hardware.

entries.name: Exposure of Sensitive System Information Due to Uncleared Debug Information
entries.text: The hardware product enters debug mode but does not fully clear security-sensitive values, such as keys and intermediate values in cryptographic operations.

entries.name: Improper Restriction of Security Token Assignment
entries.text: The System-On-A-Chip (SoC) implements a Security Token mechanism to differentiate what actions are allowed or disallowed when a transaction originates from an entity. However, the Security Tokens are improperly protected, such as improperly restricting the assignment to trusted components.
terms: Improper Restriction of Security Token Assignment

entries.name: Buffer Over-read
entries.text: The product reads from a buffer using buffer access mechanisms such as indexes or pointers that reference memory locations after the targeted buffer.

entries.name: Improper Handling of Overlap Between Protected Memory Ranges
entries.text: The product allows address regions to overlap, which can result in the bypassing of intended memory protection.

entries.name: Improper Handling of Single Event Upsets
entries.text: The hardware logic does not effectively handle when single-event upsets (SEUs) occur.
terms: Improper Handling of Single Event Upsets

entries.name: Improper Access Control for Register Interface
entries.text: The product uses memory-mapped I/O registers that act as an interface to hardware functionality from software, but there is improper access control to those registers.
terms: Improper Access Control for Register Interface

entries.name: Improper Physical Access Control
entries.text: The product is designed with access restricted to certain information, but it does not sufficiently protect against an unauthorized actor with physical access to these areas.

entries.name: Hardware Logic with Insecure De-Synchronization between Control and Data Channels
entries.text: The hardware logic for error handling and security checks can incorrectly forward data before the security check is complete.

entries.name: Unintended Reentrant Invocation of Non-reentrant Code Via Nested Calls
entries.text: The product invokes code that is believed to be reentrant, but the code performs a call that unintentionally produces a nested invocation of non-reentrant code.

entries.name: Improper Scrubbing of Sensitive Data from Decommissioned Device
entries.text: The product does not properly provide a capability for the product administrator to remove sensitive data at the time the product is decommissioned. A scrubbing capability could be missing, insufficient, or incorrect.

entries.name: Policy Uses Obsolete Encoding
entries.text: The product uses an encoding mechanism that is no longer trusted, i.e., an obsolete encoding, to implement access controls.

entries.name: Policy Privileges are not Assigned Consistently Between Control and Data Agents
entries.text: The product's hardware-enforced access control for a particular resource improperly accounts for privilege discrepancies between control and write policies.

entries.name: Product Released in Non-Release Configuration
entries.text: The product released to market is released in pre-production or manufacturing configuration.

entries.name: Buffer Under-read
entries.text: The product reads from a buffer using buffer access mechanisms such as indexes or pointers that reference memory locations prior to the targeted buffer.

entries.name: Generation of Incorrect Security Tokens
entries.text: The product implements a Security Token mechanism to differentiate what actions are allowed or disallowed when a transaction originates from an entity. However, the Security Tokens generated in the system are incorrect.

entries.name: Uninitialized Value on Reset for Registers Holding Security Settings
entries.text: Security-critical logic is not set to a known value on reset.

entries.name: Sensitive Information Uncleared Before Debug/Power State Transition
entries.text: The product performs a power or debug state transition, but it does not clear sensitive information that should no longer be accessible due to changes to information access restrictions.

entries.name: Device Unlock Credential Sharing
entries.text: The credentials necessary for unlocking a device are shared across multiple parties and may expose sensitive information.

entries.name: Improper Access Control for Volatile Memory Containing Boot Code
entries.text: The product conducts a secure-boot process that transfers bootloader code from Non-Volatile Memory (NVM) into Volatile Memory (VM), but it does not have sufficient access control or other protections for the Volatile Memory.

entries.name: Sensitive Cookie with Improper SameSite Attribute
entries.text: The SameSite attribute for sensitive cookies is not set, or an insecure value is used.
terms: Sensitive Cookie with Improper SameSite Attribute

entries.name: Hardware Child Block Incorrectly Connected to Parent System
entries.text: Signals between a hardware IP and the parent system design are incorrectly connected.

entries.name: Firmware Not Updateable
entries.text: The product does not provide its users with the ability to update or patch its firmware to address any vulnerabilities or weaknesses that may be present.

entries.name: Missing Protection Against Hardware Reverse Engineering Using Integrated Circuit (IC) Imaging Techniques
entries.text: Information stored in hardware may be recovered by an attacker with the capability to capture and analyze images of the integrated circuit using techniques such as scanning electron microscopy.

entries.name: Cryptographic Operations are Run Before Supporting Units are Ready
entries.text: Performing cryptographic operations without ensuring that the supporting inputs are ready to supply valid data may compromise the cryptographic result.

entries.name: Wrap-around Error
entries.text: Wrap around errors occur whenever a value is incremented past the maximum value for its type and therefore "wraps around" to a very small, negative, or undefined value.

entries.name: Access Control Check Implemented After Asset is Accessed
entries.text: A product's hardware-based access control check occurs after the asset has been accessed.

entries.name: Sequence of Processor Instructions Leads to Unexpected Behavior
entries.text: Specific combinations of processor instructions lead to undesirable behavior such as locking the processor until a hard reset performed.

entries.name: Assumed-Immutable Data is Stored in Writable Memory
entries.text: Immutable data, such as a first-stage bootloader, device identifiers, and "write-once" configuration settings are stored in writable memory that can be re-programmed or updated in the field.

entries.name: Mutable Attestation or Measurement Reporting Data
entries.text: The register contents used for attestation or measurement reporting data to verify boot flow are modifiable by an adversary.
terms: Mutable Attestation or Measurement Reporting Data

entries.name: Improper Validation of Specified Quantity in Input
entries.text: The product receives input that is expected to specify a quantity (such as size or length), but it does not validate or incorrectly validates that the quantity has the required properties.

entries.name: Improper Validation of Specified Index, Position, or Offset in Input
entries.text: The product receives input that is expected to specify an index, position, or offset into an indexable resource such as a buffer or file, but it does not validate or incorrectly validates that the specified index/position/offset has the required properties.

entries.name: Improper Validation of Syntactic Correctness of Input
entries.text: The product receives input that is expected to be well-formed - i.e., to comply with a certain syntax - but it does not validate or incorrectly validates that the input complies with the syntax.

entries.name: Improper Validation of Specified Type of Input
entries.text: The product receives input that is expected to be of a certain type, but it does not validate or incorrectly validates that the input is actually of the expected type.

entries.name: Improper Validation of Consistency within Input
entries.text: The product receives a complex input with multiple elements or fields that must be consistent with each other, but it does not validate or incorrectly validates that the input is actually consistent.
terms: Improper Validation of Consistency within Input

entries.name: Improper Validation of Unsafe Equivalence in Input
entries.text: The product receives an input value that is used as a resource identifier or other type of reference, but it does not validate or incorrectly validates that the input is equivalent to a potentially-unsafe value.

entries.name: Improper Validation of Array Index
entries.text: The product uses untrusted input when calculating or using an array index, but the product does not validate or incorrectly validates the index to ensure the index references a valid position within the array.

entries.name: Incorrect Decoding of Security Identifiers
entries.text: The product implements a decoding mechanism to decode certain bus-transaction signals to security identifiers, but it decodes an untrusted agent's security identifier into a trusted agent's security identifier.

entries.name: Public Key Re-Use for Signing both Debug and Production Code
entries.text: The same public key is used for signing both debug and production code.

entries.name: Incorrect Conversion of Security Identifiers
entries.text: The product implements a conversion mechanism to map certain bus-transaction signals to security identifiers, but this conversion between protocols is incorrectly implemented.

entries.name: Missing Source Correlation of Multiple Independent Data
entries.text: The product relies on one source of data, preventing the ability to detect if an adversary has compromised a data source.

entries.name: Insecure Security Identifier Mechanism
entries.text: The System-on-Chip (SoC) implements a Security Identifier mechanism to differentiate what actions are allowed or disallowed when a transaction originates from an entity. However, the Security Identifiers are not correctly implemented.

entries.name: Debug Messages Revealing Unnecessary Information
entries.text: The product fails to adequately prevent the revealing of unnecessary and potentially sensitive system information within debugging messages.

entries.name: Incorrect Chaining or Granularity of Debug Components
entries.text: The product's debug components contain incorrect chaining or granularity of debug components.

entries.name: Unprotected Confidential Information on Device is Accessible by OSAT Vendors
entries.text: The product does not adequately protect confidential information on the device from being accessed by Outsourced Semiconductor Assembly and Test (OSAT) vendors.

entries.name: Hardware Logic Contains Race Conditions
entries.text: A race condition in the hardware logic results in undermining security guarantees of the system.

entries.name: Missing Protection Mechanism for Alternate Hardware Interface
entries.text: The lack of protections on alternate paths to access control-protected assets (such as unprotected shadow registers and other external facing unguarded interfaces) allows an attacker to bypass existing protections to the asset that are only performed against the primary path.

entries.name: ASP.NET Misconfiguration: Password in Configuration File
entries.text: Storing a plaintext password in a configuration file allows anyone who can read the file access to the password-protected resource making them an easy target for attackers.

entries.name: Length manipulation
entries.title: Improper Handling of Length Parameter Inconsistency
entries.text: The product parses a formatted message or structure, but it does not handle or incorrectly handles a length field that is inconsistent with the actual length of the associated data.
terms: Improper Handling of Length Parameter Inconsistency

entries.name: Improper Protection of Physical Side Channels
entries.text: The device does not contain sufficient protection mechanisms to prevent physical side channels from exposing sensitive information due to patterns in physically observable phenomena such as variations in power consumption, electromagnetic emissions (EME), or acoustic emissions.
terms: Improper Protection of Physical Side Channels

entries.name: Insufficient or Incomplete Data Removal within Hardware Component
entries.text: The product's data removal process does not completely delete all data and potentially sensitive information within hardware components.

entries.name: Missing Source Identifier in Entity Transactions on a System-On-Chip (SOC)
entries.text: The product implements a security identifier mechanism to differentiate what actions are allowed or disallowed when a transaction originates from an entity, but the entity does not consistently include the necessary Security Identifier with a security-critical transaction.

entries.name: Non-Transparent Sharing of Microarchitectural Resources
entries.text: Hardware structures shared across execution contexts (e.g., caches and branch predictors) can violate the expected architecture isolation between contexts.

entries.name: Improperly Preserved Integrity of Hardware Configuration State During a Power Save/Restore Operation
entries.text: The product performs a power save/restore operation, but it does not ensure that the integrity of the configuration state is maintained and/or verified between the beginning and ending of the operation.

entries.name: Incorrect Calculation of Buffer Size
entries.text: The product does not correctly calculate the size to be used when allocating a buffer.

entries.name: Missing Ability to Patch ROM Code
entries.text: Missing an ability to patch ROM code may leave a System or System-on-Chip (SoC) in a vulnerable state.
terms: Missing Ability to Patch ROM Code

entries.name: Improper Translation of Security Attributes by Fabric Bridge
entries.text: The fabric bridge incorrectly translates security attributes from either trusted to untrusted or from untrusted to trusted when converting from one fabric protocol to another.

entries.name: Missing Protection for Mirrored Regions in On-Chip Fabric Firewall
entries.text: The firewall in an on-chip fabric protects the main addressed region, but it does not protect any mirrored memory or memory-mapped-IO (MMIO) regions.

entries.name: Hardware Allows Activation of Test or Debug Logic at Runtime
entries.text: During runtime, the hardware allows for test or debug logic (feature) to be activated, which allows for changing the state of the hardware. This feature can alter the intended behavior of the system and allow for alteration and leakage of sensitive data by an adversary.

entries.name: Missing Write Protection for Parametric Data Values
entries.text: The device does not write-protect the parametric data values for sensors that scale the sensor value, allowing untrusted software to manipulate the apparent result and potentially damage hardware or cause operational failure.

entries.name: Improper Setting of Bus Controlling Capability in Fabric End-point
entries.text: The bus controller enables bits in the fabric end-point to allow responder devices to control transactions on the fabric.

entries.name: Fabric-Address Map Allows Programming of Unwarranted Overlaps of Protected and Unprotected Ranges
entries.text: The address map of the on-chip fabric has protected and unprotected regions overlapping, allowing an attacker to bypass access control to the overlapping portion of the protected region.

entries.name: Improper Access Control in Fabric Bridge
entries.text: The product uses a fabric bridge for transactions between two Intellectual Property (IP) blocks, but the bridge does not properly perform the expected privilege, identity, or other access control checks between those IP blocks.
terms: Improper Access Control in Fabric Bridge

entries.name: Missing Support for Security Features in On-chip Fabrics or Buses
entries.text: On-chip fabrics or buses either do not support or are not configured to support privilege separation or other security features, such as access control.

entries.name: Improper Protection against Electromagnetic Fault Injection (EM-FI)
entries.text: The device is susceptible to electromagnetic fault injection attacks, causing device internal information to be compromised or security mechanisms to be bypassed.
terms: Improper Protection against Electromagnetic Fault Injection

entries.name: Improper Protection for Outbound Error Messages and Alert Signals
entries.text: Untrusted agents can disable alerts about signal conditions exceeding limits or the response mechanism that handles such alerts.

entries.name: Prototype Pollution
entries.title: Improperly Controlled Modification of Object Prototype Attributes
entries.text: The product receives input from an upstream component that specifies attributes that are to be initialized or updated in an object, but it does not properly control modifications of attributes of the object prototype.

entries.name: Use of Blocking Code in Single-threaded, Non-blocking Context
entries.text: The product uses a non-blocking model that relies on a single threaded process for features such as scalability, but it contains code that can block when it is invoked.

entries.name: Improper Management of Sensitive Trace Data
entries.text: Trace data collected from several sources on the System-on-Chip (SoC) is stored in unprotected locations or transported to untrusted agents.
terms: Improper Management of Sensitive Trace Data

entries.name: Improperly Controlled Sequential Memory Allocation
entries.text: The product manages a group of objects or resources and performs a separate memory allocation for each object, but it does not properly limit the total amount of memory that is consumed by all of the combined objects.

entries.name: Missing Immutable Root of Trust in Hardware
entries.text: A missing immutable root of trust in the hardware results in the ability to bypass secure boot or execute untrusted or adversarial boot code.

entries.name: Binding to an Unrestricted IP Address
entries.text: The product assigns the address 0.0.0.0 for a database server, a cloud service/instance, or any computing resource that communicates remotely.
terms: Binding to an Unrestricted IP Address

entries.name: Security Version Number Mutable to Older Versions
entries.text: The security version number in the hardware product is mutable, resulting in the ability to downgrade (roll-back) the boot firmware to vulnerable code versions.

entries.name: Reliance on Component That is Not Updateable
entries.text: The product contains a component that cannot be updated or patched in order to remove vulnerabilities or significant bugs.

entries.name: Remanent Data Readable after Memory Erase
entries.text: Confidential information stored in memory circuits is readable or recoverable after being cleared or erased, i.e., there is data remanence.
terms: Remanent Data Readable after Memory Erase

entries.name: Improper Isolation of Shared Resources in Network On Chip (NoC)
entries.text: The Network On Chip (NoC) does not isolate or incorrectly isolates its on-chip-fabric and internal resources such that they are shared between trusted and untrusted agents, creating timing channels.

entries.name: Improper Handling of Faults that Lead to Instruction Skips
entries.text: The device is missing or incorrectly implements circuitry or sensors that detect and mitigate the skipping of security-critical CPU instructions when they occur.

entries.name: Inefficient Regular Expression Complexity
entries.text: The product uses a regular expression with a worst-case computational complexity that is inefficient and possibly exponential.

entries.name: Unauthorized Error Injection Can Degrade Hardware Redundancy
entries.text: An unauthorized agent can inject errors into a redundant block to deprive the system of redundancy or put the system in a degraded operating mode.

entries.name: Incorrect Bitwise Shift of Integer
entries.text: An integer value is specified to be shifted by a negative amount or an amount greater than or equal to the number of bits contained in the value.

entries.name: Server-Side Template Injection / SSTI
entries.title: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a Template Engine
entries.text: The product uses a template engine to insert or process externally-influenced input, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special elements or syntax that can be interpreted as template expressions or other code directives when processed by the engine.

entries.name: Improper Protections Against Hardware Overheating
entries.text: A hardware device is missing or has inadequate protection features to prevent overheating.

entries.name: Insufficient Precision or Accuracy of a Real Number
entries.text: The product processes a real number with an implementation in which the number's representation does not preserve required accuracy and precision in its fractional part, causing an incorrect result.

entries.name: Use of Externally-Controlled Format String
entries.text: The product uses a function that accepts a format string as an argument, but the format string originates from an external source.

entries.name: Multiple Releases of Same Resource or Handle
entries.text: The product attempts to close or release a resource or handle more than once, without any successful open between the close operations.

entries.name: Information Exposure through Microarchitectural State after Transient Execution
entries.text: The processor does not properly clear microarchitectural state after incorrect microcode assists or speculative execution, resulting in transient execution.

entries.name: Incorrect Calculation of Multi-Byte String Length
entries.text: The product does not correctly calculate the length of strings that can contain wide or multi-byte characters.

entries.name: Improper Handling of Hardware Behavior in Exceptionally Cold Environments
entries.text: The hardware device, or the firmware running on it, is missing or has incorrect protection mechanisms to maintain goals of security primitives when the device is cooled below standard operating temperatures.

entries.name: Reliance on Insufficiently Trustworthy Component
entries.text: The product is built from multiple separate components, but it uses a component that is not sufficiently trusted to meet expectations for security, reliability, updateability, and maintainability.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements
entries.text: The product receives input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special elements that could be interpreted as control elements or syntactic markers when they are sent to a downstream component.

entries.name: Improper Handling of Physical or Environmental Conditions
entries.text: The product does not properly handle unexpected physical or environmental conditions that occur naturally or are artificially induced.

entries.name: Missing Origin Validation in WebSockets
entries.text: The product uses a WebSocket, but it does not properly verify that the source of data or communication is valid.

entries.name: Insecure Operation on Windows Junction / Mount Point
entries.text: The product opens a file or directory, but it does not properly prevent the name from being associated with a junction or mount point to a destination that is outside of the intended control sphere.

entries.name: Incorrect Parsing of Numbers with Different Radices
entries.text: The product parses numeric input assuming base 10 (decimal) values, but it does not account for inputs that use a different base number (radix).

entries.name: Weak Authentication
entries.text: The product uses an authentication mechanism to restrict access to specific users or identities, but the mechanism does not sufficiently prove that the claimed identity is correct.

entries.name: Use of Weak Credentials
entries.text: The product uses weak credentials (such as a default key or hard-coded password) that can be calculated, derived, reused, or guessed by an attacker.

entries.name: Use of Default Credentials
entries.text: The product uses default credentials (such as passwords or cryptographic keys) for potentially critical functionality.

entries.name: Use of Default Password
entries.text: The product uses default passwords for potentially critical functionality.

entries.name: Use of Default Cryptographic Key
entries.text: The product uses a default cryptographic key for potentially critical functionality.

entries.name: Dependency on Vulnerable Third-Party Component
entries.text: The product has a dependency on a third-party component that contains one or more known vulnerabilities.

entries.name: Compiler Removal of Code to Clear Buffers
entries.text: Sensitive memory is cleared according to the source code, but compiler optimizations leave the memory untouched when it is not read from again, aka "dead store removal."

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Delimiters
entries.text: The product does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes delimiters.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Parameter/Argument Delimiters
entries.text: The product receives input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special elements that could be interpreted as parameter or argument delimiters when they are sent to a downstream component.

entries.name: Incorrect Initialization of Resource
entries.text: The product attempts to initialize a resource but does not correctly do so, which might leave the resource in an unexpected, incorrect, or insecure state when it is accessed.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Value Delimiters
entries.text: The product receives input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special elements that could be interpreted as value delimiters when they are sent to a downstream component.

entries.name: Exposure of Sensitive Information during Transient Execution
entries.text: A processor event or prediction may allow incorrect operations (or correct operations with incorrect data) to execute transiently, potentially exposing data over a covert channel.

entries.name: Exposure of Sensitive Information in Shared Microarchitectural Structures during Transient Execution
entries.text: A processor event may allow transient operations to access architecturally restricted data (for example, in another address space) in a shared microarchitectural structure (for example, a CPU cache), potentially exposing the data over a covert channel.

entries.name: Exposure of Sensitive Information caused by Incorrect Data Forwarding during Transient Execution
entries.text: A processor event or prediction may allow incorrect or stale data to be forwarded to transient operations, potentially exposing data over a covert channel.

entries.name: Exposure of Sensitive Information caused by Shared Microarchitectural Predictor State that Influences Transient Execution
entries.text: Shared microarchitectural predictor state may allow code to influence transient execution across a hardware boundary, potentially exposing data that is accessible beyond the boundary over a covert channel.

entries.name: Improper Validation of Generative AI Output
entries.text: The product invokes a generative AI/ML component whose behaviors and outputs cannot be directly controlled, but the product does not validate or insufficiently validates the outputs to ensure that they align with the intended security, content, or privacy policy.
terms: Improper Validation of Generative AI Output

entries.name: Prompt injection
entries.title: Improper Neutralization of Input Used for LLM Prompting
entries.text: The product uses externally-provided data to build prompts provided to large language models (LLMs), but the way these prompts are constructed causes the LLM to fail to distinguish between user-supplied inputs and developer provided system directives.

entries.name: Reliance on HTTP instead of HTTPS
entries.text: The product provides or relies on use of HTTP communications when HTTPS is available.
terms: Reliance on HTTP instead of HTTPS

entries.name: Missing Security-Relevant Feedback for Unexecuted Operations in Hardware Interface
entries.text: The product has a hardware interface that silently discards operations in situations for which feedback would be security-relevant, such as the timely detection of failures or attacks.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Record Delimiters
entries.text: The product receives input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special elements that could be interpreted as record delimiters when they are sent to a downstream component.

entries.name: Driving Intermediate Cryptographic State/Results to Hardware Module Outputs
entries.text: The product uses a hardware module implementing a cryptographic algorithm that writes sensitive information about the intermediate state or results of its cryptographic operations via one of its output wires (typically the output port containing the final result).

entries.name: Insecure Setting of Generative AI/ML Model Inference Parameters
entries.text: The product has a component that relies on a generative AI/ML model configured with inference parameters that produce an unacceptably high rate of erroneous or unexpected outputs.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Line Delimiters
entries.text: The product receives input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special elements that could be interpreted as line delimiters when they are sent to a downstream component.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Section Delimiters
entries.text: The product receives input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special elements that could be interpreted as section delimiters when they are sent to a downstream component.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Expression/Command Delimiters
entries.text: The product receives input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special elements that could be interpreted as expression or command delimiters when they are sent to a downstream component.

entries.name: Hardware Simulation / Synthesis Mismatch
entries.text: The hardware design contains structures that are interpreted differently during synthesis than during simulation, which cause inconsistencies in security-relevant behavior between the synthesized implementation and the simulation.

entries.name: Improper Session Management
entries.text: The product does not properly manage user-related sessions such as setting appropriate configurations and settings for sessions on creation and handling sessions throughout their lifetime.

entries.name: Insufficient Session Timeout Value
entries.text: The product establishes an authenticated user session, but it does not properly set a timeout for the session. That is, the timeout is set to an excessively large value or is not set at all.

entries.name: Improper Session Invalidation
entries.text: The product establishes a session for an authenticated user, but it does not properly invalidate or terminate the session when it is required.

entries.name: Improper Session Invalidation after User Logout
entries.text: The product provides a logout functionality or otherwise attempts to end an active session for a user, but it does not properly invalidate the session upon logout.
terms: Improper Session Invalidation after User Logout

entries.name: Improper Session Invalidation after Authentication Credential Change
entries.text: The product provides a capability for users to change their authentication credentials, such as username or password, but it does not properly invalidate any current authenticated sessions after this authentication credential change.

entries.name: Use of Singular Authentication Artifact for Multiple User Sessions
entries.text: The product provides an authentication artifact, such as an authentication token, for an authenticated user session, but the same artifact is used for every authenticated user session, potentially across multiple different applications.

entries.name: Improper Check for Credential Expiration
entries.text: The product receives a request that includes a credential such as a key, certificate, password, confirmation code, or token, but the product does not check whether the credential is expired.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Input Terminators
entries.text: The product receives input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special elements that could be interpreted as input terminators when they are sent to a downstream component.

entries.name: Improper External Identity Verification
entries.text: The product supports user accounts that include a user's external identifier or communications channel - such as email, phone number, social media account, or domain name - but it does not properly verify that the user actually controls the associated identifier or channel.

entries.name: Insufficiently Controlled Parser Differential
entries.text: The product uses a common specification or format that is shared between multiple components or entities, but the components have different parsers that can interpret the same input in different, security-relevant ways.

entries.name: Generation of Credential with Long Expiration
entries.text: The product generates or relies on a credential such as a key, certificate, password, confirmation code, or token, but the credential does not expire or has an expiration that is too long, i.e., the expiration is insufficient for the intended security policy of the product.
terms: Generation of Credential with Long Expiration

entries.name: Improper Expiration of Cached Data
entries.text: The product uses or supports data in a cache, but it does not properly specify an expiration with a date, time, or time period that is sufficient for the intended security policy of the product or its adminstrators.

entries.name: Non-Equivalent Data Transformation
entries.text: The product parses or transforms data into another format, structure, or representation, but the newly-produced data is not semantically equivalent to the original data.

entries.name: Incomplete Data/State Propagation
entries.text: The product passes control to another component or function, or it performs a state transition, but it does not provide some security-critical data/state that is needed by the receiving component/function.

entries.name: Improper Request Propagation before Data Reception in Write Transactions in a Bus Architecture
entries.text: The product uses a multi-manager shared bus architecture with an on-chip interconnect that speculatively propagates a request for a write transaction, but it does not ensure that the remaining steps required by the manager module to complete the request are fulfilled in a timely manner.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Input Leaders
entries.text: The product does not properly handle when a leading character or sequence ("leader") is missing or malformed, or if multiple leaders are used when only one should be allowed.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Quoting Syntax
entries.text: Quotes injected into a product can be used to compromise a system. As data are parsed, an injected/absent/duplicate/malformed use of quotes may cause the process to take unexpected actions.

entries.name: External Control of System or Configuration Setting
entries.text: One or more system settings or configuration elements can be externally controlled by a user.

entries.name: ANSI injection
entries.title: Improper Neutralization of Escape, Meta, or Control Sequences
entries.text: The product receives input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special elements that could be interpreted as escape, meta, or control character sequences when they are sent to a downstream component.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Comment Delimiters
entries.text: The product receives input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special elements that could be interpreted as comment delimiters when they are sent to a downstream component.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Macro Symbols
entries.text: The product receives input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special elements that could be interpreted as macro symbols when they are sent to a downstream component.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Substitution Characters
entries.text: The product receives input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special elements that could be interpreted as substitution characters when they are sent to a downstream component.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Variable Name Delimiters
entries.text: The product receives input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special elements that could be interpreted as variable name delimiters when they are sent to a downstream component, such as a "$" that could be used to access an environment variable.
terms: Improper Neutralization of Variable Name Delimiters

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Wildcards or Matching Symbols
entries.text: The product receives input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special elements that could be interpreted as wildcards or matching symbols when they are sent to a downstream component.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Whitespace
entries.text: The product receives input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special elements that could be interpreted as whitespace when they are sent to a downstream component, e.g., space or tab.

entries.name: Failure to Sanitize Paired Delimiters
entries.text: The product does not properly handle the characters that are used to mark the beginning and ending of a group of entities, such as parentheses, brackets, and braces.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Null Byte or NUL Character
entries.text: The product receives input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes NUL characters or null bytes when they are sent to a downstream component.

entries.name: Improper Handling of Invalid Use of Special Elements
entries.text: The product does not properly filter, remove, quote, or otherwise manage the invalid use of special elements in user-controlled input, which could cause adverse effect on its behavior and integrity.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Leading Special Elements
entries.text: The product receives input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes leading special elements that could be interpreted in unexpected ways when they are sent to a downstream component.
terms: Improper Neutralization of Leading Special Elements

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Multiple Leading Special Elements
entries.text: The product receives input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes multiple leading special elements that could be interpreted in unexpected ways when they are sent to a downstream component.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Trailing Special Elements
entries.text: The product receives input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes trailing special elements that could be interpreted in unexpected ways when they are sent to a downstream component.
terms: Improper Neutralization of Trailing Special Elements

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Multiple Trailing Special Elements
entries.text: The product receives input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes multiple trailing special elements that could be interpreted in unexpected ways when they are sent to a downstream component.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Internal Special Elements
entries.text: The product receives input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes internal special elements that could be interpreted in unexpected ways when they are sent to a downstream component.
terms: Improper Neutralization of Internal Special Elements

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Multiple Internal Special Elements
entries.text: The product receives input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes multiple internal special elements that could be interpreted in unexpected ways when they are sent to a downstream component.

entries.name: Improper Handling of Missing Special Element
entries.text: The product receives input from an upstream component, but it does not handle or incorrectly handles when an expected special element is missing.
terms: Improper Handling of Missing Special Element

entries.name: Improper Handling of Additional Special Element
entries.text: The product receives input from an upstream component, but it does not handle or incorrectly handles when an additional unexpected special element is provided.
terms: Improper Handling of Additional Special Element

entries.name: Improper Handling of Inconsistent Special Elements
entries.text: The product does not properly handle input in which an inconsistency exists between two or more special characters or reserved words.
terms: Improper Handling of Inconsistent Special Elements

entries.name: Improper Null Termination
entries.text: The product does not terminate or incorrectly terminates a string or array with a null character or equivalent terminator.

entries.name: Improper Encoding or Decoding of Data
entries.text: The product does not properly encode or decode data, resulting in unexpected values that are not equivalent to the original data.
terms: Improper Encoding or Decoding of Data

entries.name: Improper Handling of Alternate Encoding
entries.text: The product does not properly handle when an input uses an alternate encoding that is valid for the control sphere to which the input is being sent.

entries.name: Double Decoding of the Same Data
entries.text: The product decodes the same input twice.
terms: Double Decoding of the Same Data

entries.name: Improper Handling of Mixed Encoding
entries.text: The product does not properly handle when the same input uses several different (mixed) encodings.

entries.name: Improper Handling of Unicode Encoding
entries.text: The product does not properly handle when an input contains Unicode encoding.

entries.name: Improper Handling of URL Encoding (Hex Encoding)
entries.text: The product does not properly handle when all or part of an input has been URL encoded.

entries.name: Improper Handling of Case Sensitivity
entries.text: The product does not properly account for differences in case sensitivity when accessing or determining the properties of a resource, leading to inconsistent results.

entries.name: Incorrect Behavior Order: Early Validation
entries.text: The product validates input before applying protection mechanisms that modify the input.

entries.name: Incorrect Behavior Order: Validate Before Canonicalize
entries.text: The product validates input before it is canonicalized.
terms: Incorrect Behavior Order: Validate Before Canonicalize

entries.name: Incorrect Behavior Order: Validate Before Filter
entries.text: The product validates data before it has been filtered, which prevents the product from detecting data that becomes invalid after the filtering step.
terms: Incorrect Behavior Order: Validate Before Filter

entries.name: Collapse of Data into Unsafe Value
entries.text: The product filters data in a way that causes it to be reduced or "collapsed" into an unsafe value that violates an expected security property.
terms: Collapse of Data into Unsafe Value

entries.name: Permissive List of Allowed Inputs
entries.text: The product implements a protection mechanism that relies on a list of inputs (or properties of inputs) that are explicitly allowed by policy because the inputs are assumed to be safe, but the list is too permissive - that is, it allows an input that is unsafe, leading to resultant weaknesses.

entries.name: Incomplete List of Disallowed Inputs
entries.text: The product implements a protection mechanism that relies on a list of inputs (or properties of inputs) that are not allowed by policy or otherwise require other action to neutralize before additional processing takes place, but the list is incomplete.

entries.name: Incorrect Regular Expression
entries.text: The product specifies a regular expression in a way that causes data to be improperly matched or compared.

entries.name: Overly Restrictive Regular Expression
entries.text: A regular expression is overly restrictive in a way that does not match all intended values.

entries.name: Partial String Comparison
entries.text: The product performs a string comparison that only examines a portion of the string before determining whether there is a match.

entries.name: Reliance on Data/Memory Layout
entries.text: The product makes invalid assumptions about how protocol data or memory is organized at a lower level.

entries.name: Integer Overflow or Wraparound
entries.text: The product performs a calculation that can produce an integer overflow or wraparound when the logic assumes that the resulting value will always be larger than the original value. This occurs when an integer value is incremented to a value that is too large to store in the associated representation. When this occurs, the value may become a very small or negative number.

entries.name: Integer Underflow (Wrap or Wraparound)
entries.text: The product subtracts one value from another, such that the result is less than the minimum allowable integer value, which produces a value that is not equal to the correct result.

entries.name: Integer Coercion Error
entries.text: Integer coercion refers to a set of flaws pertaining to the type casting, extension, or truncation of primitive data types.

entries.name: Off-by-one Error
entries.text: A product calculates or uses an incorrect maximum or minimum value that is 1 more, or 1 less, than the correct value.

entries.name: Unexpected Sign Extension
entries.text: The product performs an operation on a number that causes it to be sign extended when it is transformed into a larger data type.

entries.name: Signed to Unsigned Conversion Error
entries.text: The product uses a signed primitive and performs a cast to an unsigned primitive, which can produce an unexpected value if the value of the signed primitive can not be represented using an unsigned primitive.

entries.name: Unsigned to Signed Conversion Error
entries.text: The product uses an unsigned primitive and performs a cast to a signed primitive, which can produce an unexpected value if the value of the unsigned primitive can not be represented using a signed primitive.

entries.name: Numeric Truncation Error
entries.text: Truncation errors occur when a primitive is cast to a primitive of a smaller size and data is lost in the conversion.

entries.name: Use of Incorrect Byte Ordering
entries.text: The product receives input from an upstream component, but it does not account for byte ordering (e.g. big-endian and little-endian) when processing the input, causing an incorrect number or value to be used.

entries.name: Improper Input Validation
entries.text: The product receives input or data, but it does not validate or incorrectly validates that the input has the properties that are required to process the data safely and correctly.

entries.name: Information Disclosure
entries.title: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
entries.text: The product exposes sensitive information to an actor that is not explicitly authorized to have access to that information.

entries.name: Insertion of Sensitive Information Into Sent Data
entries.text: The code transmits data to another actor, but a portion of the data includes sensitive information that should not be accessible to that actor.

entries.name: Exposure of Sensitive Information Through Data Queries
entries.text: When trying to keep information confidential, an attacker can often infer some of the information by using statistics.

entries.name: Observable Discrepancy
entries.text: The product behaves differently or sends different responses under different circumstances in a way that is observable to an unauthorized actor.

entries.name: Observable Response Discrepancy
entries.text: The product provides different responses to incoming requests in a way that reveals internal state information to an unauthorized actor outside of the intended control sphere.

entries.name: Observable Behavioral Discrepancy
entries.text: The product's behaviors indicate important differences that may be observed by unauthorized actors in a way that reveals (1) its internal state or decision process, or (2) differences from other products with equivalent functionality.

entries.name: Observable Internal Behavioral Discrepancy
entries.text: The product performs multiple behaviors that are combined to produce a single result, but the individual behaviors are observable separately in a way that allows attackers to reveal internal state or internal decision points.

entries.name: Observable Behavioral Discrepancy With Equivalent Products
entries.text: The product operates in an environment in which its existence or specific identity should not be known, but it behaves differently than other products with equivalent functionality, in a way that is observable to an attacker.
terms: Observable Behavioral Discrepancy With Equivalent Products

entries.name: Observable Timing Discrepancy
entries.text: Two separate operations in a product require different amounts of time to complete, in a way that is observable to an actor and reveals security-relevant information about the state of the product, such as whether a particular operation was successful or not.

entries.name: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information
entries.text: The product generates an error message that includes sensitive information about its environment, users, or associated data.

entries.name: Self-generated Error Message Containing Sensitive Information
entries.text: The product identifies an error condition and creates its own diagnostic or error messages that contain sensitive information.

entries.name: Externally-Generated Error Message Containing Sensitive Information
entries.text: The product performs an operation that triggers an external diagnostic or error message that is not directly generated or controlled by the product, such as an error generated by the programming language interpreter that a software application uses. The error can contain sensitive system information.

entries.name: Improper Removal of Sensitive Information Before Storage or Transfer
entries.text: The product stores, transfers, or shares a resource that contains sensitive information, but it does not properly remove that information before the product makes the resource available to unauthorized actors.

entries.name: Exposure of Sensitive Information Due to Incompatible Policies
entries.text: The product's intended functionality exposes information to certain actors in accordance with the developer's security policy, but this information is regarded as sensitive according to the intended security policies of other stakeholders such as the product's administrator, users, or others whose information is being processed.

entries.name: Invocation of Process Using Visible Sensitive Information
entries.text: A process is invoked with sensitive command-line arguments, environment variables, or other elements that can be seen by other processes on the operating system.

entries.name: Insertion of Sensitive Information Into Debugging Code
entries.text: The product inserts sensitive information into debugging code.

entries.name: Storage of File with Sensitive Data Under Web Root
entries.text: The product stores sensitive data under the web document root with insufficient access control, which might make it accessible to untrusted parties.

entries.name: Path traversal
entries.title: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory
entries.text: The product uses external input to construct a pathname that is intended to identify a file or directory that is located underneath a restricted parent directory, but the product does not properly neutralize special elements within the pathname that can cause the pathname to resolve to a location that is outside of the restricted directory.

entries.name: Storage of File With Sensitive Data Under FTP Root
entries.text: The product stores sensitive data under the FTP server root with insufficient access control, which might make it accessible to untrusted parties.

entries.name: Information Loss or Omission
entries.text: The product does not record, or improperly records, security-relevant information that leads to an incorrect decision or hampers later analysis.

entries.name: Truncation of Security-relevant Information
entries.text: The product truncates the display, recording, or processing of security-relevant information in a way that can obscure the source or nature of an attack.

entries.name: Omission of Security-relevant Information
entries.text: The product does not record or display information that would be important for identifying the source or nature of an attack, or determining if an action is safe.

entries.name: Obscured Security-relevant Information by Alternate Name
entries.text: The product records security-relevant information according to an alternate name of the affected entity, instead of the canonical name.

entries.name: Sensitive Information in Resource Not Removed Before Reuse
entries.text: The product releases a resource such as memory or a file so that it can be made available for reuse, but it does not clear or "zeroize" the information contained in the resource before the product performs a critical state transition or makes the resource available for reuse by other entities.

entries.name: Improper Handling of Syntactically Invalid Structure
entries.text: The product does not handle or incorrectly handles input that is not syntactically well-formed with respect to the associated specification.
terms: Improper Handling of Syntactically Invalid Structure

entries.name: Improper Handling of Values
entries.text: The product does not properly handle when the expected number of values for parameters, fields, or arguments is not provided in input, or if those values are undefined.

entries.name: Relative Path Traversal
entries.text: The product uses external input to construct a pathname that should be within a restricted directory, but it does not properly neutralize sequences such as ".." that can resolve to a location that is outside of that directory.

entries.name: Improper Handling of Missing Values
entries.text: The product does not handle or incorrectly handles when a parameter, field, or argument name is specified, but the associated value is missing, i.e. it is empty, blank, or null.

entries.name: Improper Handling of Extra Values
entries.text: The product does not handle or incorrectly handles when more values are provided than expected.

entries.name: Improper Handling of Undefined Values
entries.text: The product does not handle or incorrectly handles when a value is not defined or supported for the associated parameter, field, or argument name.

entries.name: Improper Handling of Parameters
entries.text: The product does not properly handle when the expected number of parameters, fields, or arguments is not provided in input, or if those parameters are undefined.

entries.name: Failure to Handle Missing Parameter
entries.text: If too few arguments are sent to a function, the function will still pop the expected number of arguments from the stack. Potentially, a variable number of arguments could be exhausted in a function as well.

entries.name: Improper Handling of Extra Parameters
entries.text: The product does not handle or incorrectly handles when the number of parameters, fields, or arguments with the same name exceeds the expected amount.

entries.name: Improper Handling of Undefined Parameters
entries.text: The product does not handle or incorrectly handles when a particular parameter, field, or argument name is not defined or supported by the product.

entries.name: Improper Handling of Structural Elements
entries.text: The product does not handle or incorrectly handles inputs that are related to complex structures.

entries.name: Improper Handling of Incomplete Structural Elements
entries.text: The product does not handle or incorrectly handles when a particular structural element is not completely specified.
terms: Improper Handling of Incomplete Structural Elements

entries.name: Failure to Handle Incomplete Element
entries.text: The product does not properly handle when a particular element is not completely specified.

entries.name: Path Traversal: '../filedir'
entries.text: The product uses external input to construct a pathname that should be within a restricted directory, but it does not properly neutralize "../" sequences that can resolve to a location that is outside of that directory.

entries.name: Improper Handling of Inconsistent Structural Elements
entries.text: The product does not handle or incorrectly handles when two or more structural elements should be consistent, but are not.
terms: Improper Handling of Inconsistent Structural Elements

entries.name: Improper Handling of Unexpected Data Type
entries.text: The product does not handle or incorrectly handles when a particular element is not the expected type, e.g. it expects a digit (0-9) but is provided with a letter (A-Z).
terms: Improper Handling of Unexpected Data Type

entries.name: Use of Inherently Dangerous Function
entries.text: The product calls a function that can never be guaranteed to work safely, regardless of how it is used.

entries.name: Creation of chroot Jail Without Changing Working Directory
entries.text: The product uses the chroot() system call to create a jail, but it does not change the working directory afterward.

entries.name: Heap Inspection
entries.title: Improper Clearing of Heap Memory Before Release
entries.text: The product uses realloc() to resize buffers that contain sensitive information.

entries.name: J2EE Bad Practices: Direct Management of Connections
entries.text: The J2EE application directly manages connections, instead of using the container's connection management facilities.

entries.name: J2EE Bad Practices: Direct Use of Sockets
entries.text: The J2EE application directly uses sockets instead of using framework method calls.

entries.name: Uncaught Exception
entries.text: An exception is thrown from a function, but it is not caught.

entries.name: Path Traversal: '/../filedir'
entries.text: The product uses external input to construct a pathname that should be within a restricted directory, but it does not properly neutralize "/../" sequences that can resolve to a location that is outside of that directory.

entries.name: Execution with Unnecessary Privileges
entries.text: The product performs an operation at a privilege level that is higher than the minimum level required, which creates new weaknesses or amplifies the consequences of other weaknesses.

entries.name: Unchecked Return Value
entries.text: The product does not check the return value from a method or function.

entries.name: Incorrect Check of Function Return Value
entries.text: The product incorrectly checks a return value from a function, which prevents it from detecting errors or exceptional conditions.
terms: Incorrect Check of Function Return Value

entries.name: Plaintext Storage of a Password
entries.text: The product stores a password in plaintext within resources such as memory or files.

entries.name: Storing Passwords in a Recoverable Format
entries.text: The storage of passwords in a recoverable format makes them subject to password reuse attacks by malicious users. In fact, it should be noted that recoverable encrypted passwords provide no significant benefit over plaintext passwords since they are subject not only to reuse by malicious attackers but also by malicious insiders.
terms: Storing Passwords in a Recoverable Format

entries.name: Empty Password in Configuration File
entries.text: Using an empty string as a password is insecure.

entries.name: Use of Hard-coded Password
entries.text: The product contains a hard-coded password, which it uses for its own inbound authentication or for outbound authentication to external components.

entries.name: Path Traversal: '/dir/../filename'
entries.text: The product uses external input to construct a pathname that should be within a restricted directory, but it does not properly neutralize "/dir/../filename" sequences that can resolve to a location that is outside of that directory.

entries.name: Password in Configuration File
entries.text: The product stores a password in a configuration file that might be accessible to actors who do not know the password.

entries.name: Weak Encoding for Password
entries.text: The product uses a weak or trivial encoding for a password.

entries.name: Not Using Password Aging
entries.text: The product does not have a mechanism in place for managing password aging.

entries.name: Password Aging with Long Expiration
entries.text: The product supports password aging, but the expiration period is too long.

entries.name: Incorrect Privilege Assignment
entries.text: A product incorrectly assigns a privilege to a particular actor, creating an unintended sphere of control for that actor.

entries.name: Privilege Defined With Unsafe Actions
entries.text: A particular privilege, role, capability, or right can be used to perform unsafe actions that were not intended, even when it is assigned to the correct entity.

entries.name: Privilege Chaining
entries.text: Two distinct privileges, roles, capabilities, or rights can be combined in a way that allows an entity to perform unsafe actions that would not be allowed without that combination.

entries.name: Improper Privilege Management
entries.text: The product does not properly assign, modify, track, or check privileges for an actor, creating an unintended sphere of control for that actor.

entries.name: Path Traversal: 'dir/../../filename'
entries.text: The product uses external input to construct a pathname that should be within a restricted directory, but it does not properly neutralize multiple internal "../" sequences that can resolve to a location that is outside of that directory.

entries.name: Privilege Context Switching Error
entries.text: The product does not properly manage privileges while it is switching between different contexts that have different privileges or spheres of control.

entries.name: Privilege Dropping / Lowering Errors
entries.text: The product does not drop privileges before passing control of a resource to an actor that does not have those privileges.

entries.name: Least Privilege Violation
entries.text: The elevated privilege level required to perform operations such as chroot() should be dropped immediately after the operation is performed.

entries.name: Improper Check for Dropped Privileges
entries.text: The product attempts to drop privileges but does not check or incorrectly checks to see if the drop succeeded.

entries.name: Improper Handling of Insufficient Privileges
entries.text: The product does not handle or incorrectly handles when it has insufficient privileges to perform an operation.

entries.name: Incorrect Default Permissions
entries.text: During installation, installed file permissions are set to allow anyone to modify those files.

entries.name: Insecure Inherited Permissions
entries.text: A product defines a set of insecure permissions that are inherited by objects that are created by the program.

entries.name: Insecure Preserved Inherited Permissions
entries.text: A product inherits a set of insecure permissions for an object, e.g. when copying from an archive file, without user awareness or involvement.

entries.name: Incorrect Execution-Assigned Permissions
entries.text: While it is executing, the product sets the permissions of an object in a way that violates the intended permissions that have been specified by the user.

entries.name: Path Traversal: '..\filedir'
entries.text: The product uses external input to construct a pathname that should be within a restricted directory, but it does not properly neutralize "..\" sequences that can resolve to a location that is outside of that directory.

entries.name: Improper Handling of Insufficient Permissions or Privileges
entries.text: The product does not handle or incorrectly handles when it has insufficient privileges to access resources or functionality as specified by their permissions. This may cause it to follow unexpected code paths that may leave the product in an invalid state.

entries.name: Improper Preservation of Permissions
entries.text: The product does not preserve permissions or incorrectly preserves permissions when copying, restoring, or sharing objects, which can cause them to have less restrictive permissions than intended.

entries.name: Improper Ownership Management
entries.text: The product assigns the wrong ownership, or does not properly verify the ownership, of an object or resource.

entries.name: Unverified Ownership
entries.text: The product does not properly verify that a critical resource is owned by the proper entity.

entries.name: Improper Access Control
entries.text: The product does not restrict or incorrectly restricts access to a resource from an unauthorized actor.

entries.name: Improper Authorization
entries.text: The product does not perform or incorrectly performs an authorization check when an actor attempts to access a resource or perform an action.

entries.name: Incorrect User Management
entries.text: The product does not properly manage a user within its environment.

entries.name: Improper Authentication
entries.text: When an actor claims to have a given identity, the product does not prove or insufficiently proves that the claim is correct.

entries.name: Authentication Bypass Using an Alternate Path or Channel
entries.text: The product requires authentication, but the product has an alternate path or channel that does not require authentication.

entries.name: Authentication Bypass by Alternate Name
entries.text: The product performs authentication based on the name of a resource being accessed, or the name of the actor performing the access, but it does not properly check all possible names for that resource or actor.

entries.name: Path Traversal: '\..\filename'
entries.text: The product uses external input to construct a pathname that should be within a restricted directory, but it does not properly neutralize '\..\filename' (leading backslash dot dot) sequences that can resolve to a location that is outside of that directory.

entries.name: Authentication Bypass by Spoofing
entries.text: This attack-focused weakness is caused by incorrectly implemented authentication schemes that are subject to spoofing attacks.

entries.name: Reliance on IP Address for Authentication
entries.text: The product uses an IP address for authentication.
terms: Reliance on IP Address for Authentication

entries.name: Using Referer Field for Authentication
entries.text: The referer field in HTTP requests can be easily modified and, as such, is not a valid means of message integrity checking.

entries.name: Authentication Bypass by Capture-replay
entries.text: A capture-replay flaw exists when the design of the product makes it possible for a malicious user to sniff network traffic and bypass authentication by replaying it to the server in question to the same effect as the original message (or with minor changes).

entries.name: Improper Certificate Validation
entries.text: The product does not validate, or incorrectly validates, a certificate.

entries.name: Improper Following of a Certificate's Chain of Trust
entries.text: The product does not follow, or incorrectly follows, the chain of trust for a certificate back to a trusted root certificate.

entries.name: Improper Validation of Certificate with Host Mismatch
entries.text: The product communicates with a host that provides a certificate, but the product does not properly ensure that the certificate is actually associated with that host.

entries.name: Improper Validation of Certificate Expiration
